questions.explain: The five patterns are point lookups, tenant-time range scans, filtered vector similarity, analytical aggregations, and high-rate appends — every index and partitioning decision traces back to one of them.
options: Read, write, update, delete, and merge
Point lookups, tenant-time range scans, filtered vector similarity, analytical aggregations, high-rate appends
Full-text, vector, JSON, spatial, and graph queries
OLTP, OLAP, HTAP, streaming, and batch
questions.q: What are the five dominant access patterns AI schema design starts from?

questions.explain: Random NEWID() clustered keys cause page splits and fragmentation under sustained inserts; NEWSEQUENTIALID() keeps inserts at the end of the index on hot append tables like messages and audit logs.
options: NEWID() is required for foreign keys to work
Sequential GUIDs cannot be used as primary keys
NEWID() is faster for range scans
Random NEWID() clustered keys cause page splits and fragmentation under sustained inserts
questions.q: Why does the chapter recommend NEWSEQUENTIALID() over NEWID() for clustered keys on hot tables?

questions.explain: Documents vs. chunks (different lifecycles and indexes), conversations vs. messages (50:1 volume ratio, different query shapes), and audit as its own table (different retention and access control) — normalize on entity lifecycle.
options: By alphabetical order of entity names
By which team owns the data
By entity lifecycle: documents vs. chunks, conversations vs. messages, audit as its own table
By putting everything in one table with a type discriminator
questions.q: How does the chapter draw normalization boundaries for AI entities?

questions.explain: When two patterns conflict, a nonclustered columnstore index on top of the rowstore table gives transactional writes plus analytical scans, maintained by the engine.
options: A nonclustered columnstore index on top of the rowstore table
Two separate databases, one for each pattern
A clustered columnstore index with no rowstore
Replicating the table to a data warehouse
questions.q: When analytics wants columnstore but point lookups want rowstore, what does the chapter recommend?

questions.explain: Monthly partitioning on created_at enables partition elimination for time queries and millisecond archival via ALTER TABLE ... SWITCH PARTITION instead of deleting millions of rows.
options: It makes SELECT queries use less memory
Monthly partitioning enables partition elimination and millisecond archival via partition switch-out instead of mass DELETEs
It automatically compresses old data
It eliminates the need for indexes
questions.q: What are the benefits of partitioning hot tables by month on created_at?
